title: A quasi-finite polynomial factorization bounds the fibre dimensions on its principal open
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings with S a finite type R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let g in S and n be a natural number. Suppose f: R[t_1,...,t_n] -> S_g is an R-algebra homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-ring-localization-away], is finite type, and is quasi-finite at every prime [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. For every prime q of S not containing g, put p = q cap R and let Q be the prime of the fibre ring kappa(p) tensor_R S corresponding to q [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then the local topological Krull dimension of this fibre spectrum at Q is at most n [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point].

source.place: Proof of Tag 00QH, after the application of Tag 00QE: considering the fibres and applying Tag 00QG; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00QH and /tag/00QG because the literature checkout is not present on this machine.

proof.text: Fix a prime q of S with g outside q, and localize it to a prime qg of S_g. Its contraction to R remains p = q cap R, since the localization map factors the original R-algebra map. The given map P = R[t_1,...,t_n] to S_g is finite type and quasi-finite at every prime.

Fix $\mathfrak q'\in D(g)$ and put $\mathfrak p'=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$. Put $T=S_g\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p')$. The isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] identifies $T$ with $S_g\otimes_S(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p'))$; then [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] identifies it with $F_{\mathfrak p',\bar g}$, the localization of $F_{\mathfrak p'}=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ at $\bar g$. The base change of $P$ is $\kappa(\mathfrak p')[t_1,\dots,t_n]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension], and its map to $T$ is the base change of $P\to S_g$, by the same tensor-cancellation isomorphism with $S=P$. The latter is quasi-finite at every prime, so [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-four-rings], with $R=P$, $S=S_g$, $R'=\kappa(\mathfrak p')[t_1,\dots,t_n]$ and $S'=T$, shows that the polynomial-to-$T$ map is quasi-finite at every prime (the tensor map to $T$ is an isomorphism and hence surjective). It is of finite type because the finitely many $R$-algebra generators of $S$, together with $g^{-1}$, generate $T$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak p')[t_1,\dots,t_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00QH (lemma-dimension-fibres-bounded-open-upstairs, lines 31319-31322), 'Considering the fibres'; quasi-finite base change is Lemma Tag 00PP (lemma-quasi-finite-base-change, lines 30362-30388), through the existing four-rings form Tag 00PN

proof.text: Since $T$ is a finite type $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$-algebra with a quasi-finite map from $\kappa(\mathfrak p')[t_1,\dots,t_n]$, [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra] gives $\dim\operatorname{Spec}T\le n$. Thus the dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ at any of its points is at most $n$ by taking the whole space among the open neighbourhoods in the infimum defining local dimension [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. In particular this holds at the point $\mathfrak Q'_g$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q'_g$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00QH (lemma-dimension-fibres-bounded-open-upstairs, lines 31320-31322), via Lemma Tag 00QG (lemma-dimension-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra); local dimension bound from Topology Tag 0B7I

proof.text: Under $T\cong F_{\mathfrak p',\bar g}$ from step 2, $\operatorname{Spec}T$ is the open subspace $D(\bar g)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}F_{\mathfrak p'}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open]. The fibre-prime correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] identifies $\mathfrak Q'_g$ with the prime $\mathfrak Q'$ associated to $\mathfrak q'$; it lies in $D(\bar g)$ because $g\notin\mathfrak q'$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] gives $\dim_{\mathfrak Q'}\operatorname{Spec}F_{\mathfrak p'}=\dim_{\mathfrak Q'_g}\operatorname{Spec}T\le n$ by step 3. This is $\dim_{\mathfrak q'}(S/R)\le n$, for every $\mathfrak q'\in D(g)$.

lean.statement:
theorem fibre_dimension_le_of_quasiFinite_polynomial_localization
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [FiniteType R S] (g : S) (n : ℕ)
    (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R →ₐ[R] Localization.Away g)
    (hft : @FiniteType (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (Localization.Away g)
      _ _ f.toRingHom.toAlgebra)
    (hq : ∀ qg : PrimeSpectrum (Localization.Away g),
      @IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (Localization.Away g)
        _ _ f.toRingHom.toAlgebra hft qg)
    (q : PrimeSpectrum S) (hg : g ∉ q.asIdeal) :
    topologicalKrullDimAt
      (PrimeSpectrum.preimageEquivFiber R S (q.comap (algebraMap R S))
        ⟨q, rfl⟩) ≤ (n : WithBot ℕ∞)
